content:
maria: starting a compact field sprint doc for enterprise prospects — want a 1-page brief + 2-line benchmark blurb + webinar seed + lead-routing rules. audience: regulated fintech/healthcare. keep it skimmable.
elaine: thumbs up. include a tiny migration note (hosted -> dedicated -> private) and a tiny SLA snapshot. sales wants a line they can paste into emails.
sam: ill pull conservative benchmark stats. propose: p95 latency, per-token cost delta vs baseline self-hosted, and note on rollback safety. workload: chat + embeddings + retrieval.
raj: add control-plane/KMS note and that we support HSM. also call out automatic fallback routing for capacity/policy events.
maria: proposed structure: top blurb (problem + one-line solution), 3 proof bullets (latency, cost, uptime), deployment snapshot (TL;DR), security checkbox, micro SLA table, CTA (webinar/demo).
elaine: lead tags we need for routing: region, deploy_preference, compliance_requirement, vertical. map to AE pools.
sam: draft bullets: "p95: ~140ms on quantized 13B under standard chat profile"; "unit cost: ~0.6x baseline self-hosted with caching/batching"; "safe updates: canary rollouts + evals cut regressions in our lab tests". add footnote about test fixture (8k DAU simulated).
maria: good. make numbers conservative and add "internal lab" footnote.
raj: deployment TL;DR lines: Hosted — fastest to ship, pay-as-you-go. Dedicated — reserved GPUs, SLA-backed throughput. Private — VPC/on-prem for full control + KMS; recommended for regulated customers.
elaine: micro SLA table idea (one line each): Availability: Hosted 99.9% | Dedicated 99.95% | Private (customer infra). Latency targets p95: Hosted ~150ms | Dedicated ~100ms | Private varies. Credits: standard tiered credit policy (legal).
maria: webinar seed (short): Headline: "Reliable LLM Serving for Regulated Apps". Description: "Practical playbook: benchmarks, deployment tradeoffs, and routing patterns for high-availability regulated workloads." CTA: "Sign up — seats limited". Capture: name,email,company,region,deploy_preference,compliance_need,expected_qps.
elaine: form => map to SF via these rules. can opsbot show a tiny mapping?
opsbot: snippet: 
```yaml
lead_routing:
  - when: region == "APAC"
    owner: "APAC_AE_Pool"
  - when: deploy_preference == "private" and compliance_need == "hipaa"
    owner: "Healthcare_Specialist_AE"
  - when: deploy_preference == "dedicated" and company_size >= 1000
    owner: "Enterprise_AE_Team"
  - else:
    owner: "Growth_AE_Pool"
```
sam: benchmark narrative (short para): "In our internal lab simulating thousands of daily chat sessions and mixed retrieval calls, Redwood reduced p95 latency vs a baseline self-hosted setup while lowering per-token costs through continuous batching and prefix caching. Model-variant routing and controlled canary rollouts provided a measurable drop in update-related regressions."
maria: add a 3-line objection bank sales can copy: Security: "Private deploy + KMS/HSM + audit logs; SOC/ISO support and residency options." Cost: "Dedicated pricing + Optimize toolkit (quantize/batching) to improve unit economics." Lock-in: "Open model catalog + exportable artifacts; routing lets you mix variants."
elaine: timeline: final copy Thu COB, design assets Fri. who owns what?
maria: ill own the brief and webinar copy. elaine owns routing/SF mapping. sam finalizes numbers. raj reviews security lines.
elaine: will post mapping to /marketing/ops and tag salesops.
sam: dropping final benchmark bullets tomorrow AM.
raj: security check by Thu morning.
maria: thanks team. aim to push to field next week. opsbot: schedule campaign id "enterprise-brief-sprint-214877" start 2148805000.
elaine: :thumbsup:
